title: model-loading-breadcrumbs-scratchpad-avery-brooks
content:
Quick scratchpad for the recent model-loading failures (weights download / shard reassembly / checkpoint format). Lots of half-tests here — notes to self + breadcrumbs for on-call and RUs.

Symptoms:
- Intermittent failures when loading large models from model-store (s3). Failures seen on dedicated and private deployments.
- Common manifestations: checksum mismatch on a shard, EOF during map_file, or missing tensors in state_dict after assembling shards.

Error snippets seen (copied from logs):
- ERROR: checksum mismatch for shard-003-of-032.bin (expected: e3b0c..., got: 74a2e...)
- WARNING: safetensors header parse failed: invalid header length 0x0
- Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/workspace/serving/models/loader.py", line 342, in load_checkpoint
      sd = torch.load(shard_path, map_location=map_location)
  RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading file
- ERROR: Failed to download weights: Unexpected EOF reading object (s3://redwood-models/.../shard-012-of-032.bin)
- AssertionError: numel mismatch for tensor 'transformer.h.5.attn.q_proj.weight' (expected 7864320, got 0)
- OSError: mmap failed: Bad address (seen when using mmap on corrupted file)

Commands/troubleshooting steps already tried:
- Re-download whole model from S3 with aws cli (single-threaded):
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/my-model/ /mnt/models/my-model/ --recursive --no-guess-mime-type --only-show-errors
- Tried parallel download with aria2c for shards (to speed up) — saw increased failure rate (likely exposing flaky network).
- Verified checksums in manifest.json vs local files (sha256) with a small script (sha256sum): mismatch for 2 shards.
- Attempted to reassemble shards using our standard concat tool (cat shard-*.bin > pytorch_model.bin) — produced EOF errors on load.
- Switched loader to use safetensors loader for files with .safetensors extension; safetensors failed on 1 file with header parse error.
- Cleared local model cache (~/.cache/hf/ + /var/lib/model-cache) and re-ran download (to rule out partial cached files).
- Increased ulimit -n on nodes (in case many parallel connections caused descriptor exhaustion).
- Tried loading smaller model (same code path) — works fine. Suggests problem tied to large file handling or storage.

Hypotheses / likely root causes:
- S3 eventual consistency/partial-object during upload: some uploaded shards may have been incomplete or corrupted upstream. Need to confirm publisher side (who uploaded this model).
- Network flakiness when using parallel download (aria2c) leading to truncated files. Single-threaded aws cp more reliable.
- Bug in shard-manifest generation: manifest lists 32 shards but uploaded only 31 or sizes wrong (off-by-one in writer).
- Checkpoint format mismatch: some checkpoints were converted from older 'v1' format and paddings or metadata differ, causing loader code assumptions to break.
- safetensors/pytorch mismatch: file claimed to be safetensors but is actually a .pt (or vice versa) — loader tries wrong parser.

Repro steps to run locally (minimal):
1) On a fresh VM (Ubuntu 22.04), create /mnt/models and ensure 100GB free.
2) aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/my-model/ /mnt/models/my-model/ --recursive --no-guess-mime-type
3) verify manifest checksums: python tools/verify_manifest.py /mnt/models/my-model/manifest.json
4) attempt load with python -m repro.load_model --model-dir /mnt/models/my-model --device cpu
   - Note: repro.load_model uses mmap by default. To force direct read set env READ_WITH_MMAP=0

Useful one-liners I've run: 
- find /mnt/models/my-model -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; | sort > /tmp/local-sums.txt
- jq -r '.shards[] | [.file, .sha256] | @tsv' manifest.json > /tmp/manifest-sums.tsv
- python -c 'import sys,hashlib; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read()).hexdigest())' shard-003-of-032.bin

Observations from recent runs:
- Two specific shards (003 and 012) consistently report checksum mismatches no matter how many times downloaded.
- When I download those two shards directly from the origin bucket using gsutil (copy from different region), the checksums match the manifest. Suggests the model-store replication path (or a CDN edge) might be serving stale/corrupted copies.
- When loader switches to fallback model variant (smaller quantized model), load succeeds. Points to size/IO pressure as contributing factor.

Short-term mitigations applied:
- Added retry logic with exponential backoff to shard download routine (3 retries -> fetch from alternate region).
- If checksum mismatch after retries, mark model as quarantined and fall back to compatible variant automatically.
- Added monitoring alert (pager) for repeated manifest vs local checksum mismatches for same model id.

Open TODOs / next actions:
- [ ] Confirm uploader for my-model (who/when). Check upload pipeline logs and CI that performs shard uploads. Linked JIRA-1234 to track.
- [ ] Add server-side validation on upload: compute and store checksums atomically after upload completes.
- [ ] Investigate CDN/replication layer (edge cache) for possible partial-object serving. Work with infra team.
- [ ] Add a slow-path download that streams directly from origin (no CDN) for suspected corrupted models.
- [ ] Add end-to-end test in release CI to upload small multi-shard model and verify complete download + load.
- [ ] Fix loader to detect safetensors vs pytorch blob earlier (magic bytes) and fail-fast with clear error.
- [ ] Add size and magic-byte checks before mmap to reduce confusing mmap errors.

Notes / misc:
- Slack thread: #sre-models -> thread ts: 1723841xxxxx (see linked artifacts).
- Repro PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789 contains changes to retry + quarantine. Running canaries tomorrow.

If picking this up: start by grepping logs for these exact error substrings (checksum mismatch / unexpected EOF) and correlate with node id + region + time to see if cluster-level pattern. Then cross-ref with model-upload events (CI) around same timestamps.

End of scratchpad. Will sync with Jordan and Maya tomorrow morning.
